items.title: Indian large caps rally as November foreign inflows reverse ten months of selling
items.summary: Indian benchmark stocks rebounded while AI-heavy markets remained under pressure. Newly reported provisional institutional flows show foreign investors continued November net buying after ten months of net selling. Large-cap banks, consumer staples and pharmaceuticals led, but broader market breadth remained negative.

observations.label: November 25 local market closes, independently corroborated
Provisional institutional cash-market activity
observations.value: Foreign institutions net bought INR 4,479.08 crore; domestic institutions net bought INR 4,018.72 crore. November foreign net inflows approximately INR 1.18 trillion.

observations.label: Breadth and fundamentals
observations.value: Large-cap private banks, staples and pharma led; broader NSE decliners outnumbered advancers. Foreign inflows support relative resilience, but do not establish a broad earnings recovery.

observations.label: Risks and next indicators
observations.value: Monitor foreign cash flows, breadth, bank earnings, crude prices, proposed US tariffs and RBI policy meeting December 2–4. Renewed outflows or higher oil import costs would weaken the rotation signal.

items.key_finding: Verified local closing gains and provisional institutional cash flows support an emerging diversification signal beyond AI-heavy equities, with narrow breadth a key caveat.

items.title: AI infrastructure credit stress deepens as CoreWeave bond yields approach 18%
items.summary: Reuters reports record credit protection costs for several AI infrastructure companies, with CoreWeave's five-year credit default swap spread above 1,300 basis points. The Wall Street Journal independently corroborates elevated stress. Financing pressure could constrain future infrastructure expansion even if compute demand remains strong.

observations.label: Reuters Nov 25 report updated 10:37 AM EST
observations.value: Five-year CDS: CoreWeave 1,314 bp; Oracle 356 bp; SoftBank 501 bp (widest since October 2022). Indicative observations, not closing prices.

observations.label: Independent WSJ report Nov 25
observations.value: CoreWeave five-year CDS 1,332 bp; difference reflects separate observations. Oracle credit protection costs also elevated.

observations.label: Bond market
observations.value: Reuters: CoreWeave 2031 bond yields approached 18%; 2030 bonds reached record low prices.

observations.label: Fundamental significance
observations.value: Higher capital costs could delay marginal data-center projects and equipment orders; actual cancellations not established.

observations.label: Risks and next indicators
observations.value: Monitor financing terms, customer-backed debt, capex revisions, cash generation and backlog conversion; sustained credit-spread compression would weaken warning.

items.key_finding: Credit market stress adds independent evidence of financing risk beyond falling AI equity valuations.

sources.title: Wall Street Journal November 25 credit-market report

items.title: EIA reports third consecutive crude inventory build; energy shares resilient
items.summary: EIA reported a smaller-than-expected commercial crude inventory build, while gasoline and distillate stocks increased. Overall commercial petroleum inventories declined. Energy shares held near flat during broader equity selling, but incremental Middle Eastern export losses remain unverified.

observations.label: Nov 25 10:30 AM EST EIA, week ending Nov 20
observations.value: Commercial crude +1.1M barrels to 418.9M, 3% below five-year average; consensus +2M; gasoline +1.7M, distillate +0.7M; total commercial petroleum -2.4M barrels.

observations.label: Refining and imports
observations.value: 97.5% utilization; crude inputs 17.3M b/d; crude imports 6.2M b/d, up 673,000 b/d.

observations.label: Intraday ETF observations
observations.value: XLE +0.05% at 10:21 AM EST; XOP +0.08% at 10:32 AM EST. Different observation times; not settlements.

observations.label: Next indicators
observations.value: Saudi refinery operations, actual tanker loadings, freight and insurance, Brent/WTI settlements, Nov 29 OPEC+ meeting.

items.key_finding: US crude stocks are rebuilding, while low seasonal stocks and maritime risks leave supply vulnerable.

items.title: HP rises against broad technology selloff after earnings and dividend increase
items.summary: HP shares rose sharply after better-than-expected quarterly results and a dividend increase. Higher-value PC sales supported revenue despite falling unit shipments. Tariff refunds, memory costs and a change in adjusted earnings methodology complicate the underlying earnings comparison.

observations.label: Nov 25 10:05 AM EST Google Finance
observations.value: HPQ $30.97, +10.84%; intraday.

observations.label: Nov 24 FY26 results
observations.value: Q4 revenue $16B, +9.3% YoY; adjusted EPS $0.83, including $0.15 tariff refunds; annual FCF $3.3B; quarterly dividend $0.31.

observations.label: PC business
observations.value: Personal Systems revenue +14% YoY; units -29%; AI PCs nearly 60% of shipments; memory and storage cost pressures.

observations.label: Guidance caveat
observations.value: FY27 non-GAAP EPS $3.15–3.45; new exclusion of stock-based compensation would add $0.38 to FY26 comparable EPS; FY27 FCF $2.9–3.1B.

observations.label: Next indicators
observations.value: PC unit shipments, pricing, memory costs, margins, cash flow and normalized earnings.

items.key_finding: HP's positive earnings reaction is an outlier in tech selling, but unit weakness and accounting changes warrant caution.

sources.title: Wall Street Journal HP guidance and memory costs

items.title: Saudi-Houthi escalation raises risk to Red Sea oil-export alternatives
items.summary: Reuters reports the Saudi-led coalition struck Hodeidah port infrastructure after Houthi threats against Saudi Red Sea ports. The escalation threatens alternative export routes used amid Hormuz restrictions. Oil prices remain sensitive to both geopolitical risks and recovering supply; incremental Saudi export losses have not been verified.

observations.label: November 25 coalition statement
observations.value: Coalition reported strikes at Hodeidah after Houthi threats against Saudi Red Sea ports; damage and operational effects not independently established.

observations.label: Oil market context
observations.value: WSJ reports Brent $91.10 (-0.3%) and WTI $81.50 (-0.7%) in Wednesday trading; precise observation time not specified, not settlement.

observations.label: API estimate Nov 24
observations.value: Crude build 126,000 barrels versus 900,000 expected; secondary calendar source, pending EIA confirmation.

observations.label: Next indicators
observations.value: Saudi terminal operations, independent tanker loadings, insurance and freight, EIA 10:30 AM EST release and Nov 29 OPEC+ meeting. Stable exports would weaken disruption concern.

items.key_finding: Escalation threatens a critical alternative export corridor but does not establish incremental physical oil losses.
